title: Are Markets Wrong About the Fed? Watch This Next, Says Ilya Spivak
speaker: Ilya Spivak

macro_themes.view: UMich sentiment 46.3 (2nd worst ever, current conditions record low), GDPNow sliding to 3.6%, and breakevens not following oil all point to a growth-scare window.
Markets ~80/20 hold in October; markets price ~50bp more hikes in H1 2027 than the Fed, which could unwind if core CPI/PPI come in soft.

CPI Wednesday expected headline 3.4->3.7% y/y, core 2.4->2.5%; PPI Thursday; retail sales expected +0.3%; Fed Chair Warsh speaks with IMF chief. Watching for diminishing demand-pull inflation under the war-driven supply shock.
Long-end yields are driven partly by governments and hyperscalers competing for loanable funds; the OpenAI revenue scare gave bonds a shove higher.
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Hormuz tankers popped crude; inflation-trade dynamics weigh on gold and silver short term.
